data.narrative:
Quantum Machines is a Series C quantum computing company that has raised $280M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of 11 peers: 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the quantum computing sector. While 8 same-sector peers exist, none satisfied the narrow filtering criteria (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) required to generate three or more reliable datapoints. A stage-progression method was therefore applied, using the $280M total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series C-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.7x, yielding $476M.

Given the methodological constraints imposed by sector immaturity and sparse comparable data, the analysis supports a valuation range of $405M (low) to $547M (high), centered on $476M. The range reflects uncertainty inherent in single-method triangulation and the nascent, heterogeneous nature of the quantum computing sector, where traditional scaling patterns may not hold uniformly across hardware platforms and applications. Primary uncertainties include the applicability of standard venture step-up multiples to deep-tech hardware companies and the absence of mature public market precedent for this stage and sector.
